proposal.title: 1978–79 external peripherals — storage subsystems, controllers and mechanisms 1
proposal.reason: Import 14 distinct commercial identities from research items 1, 16, 18, 25, 26, 27, 28, 31, 33, 41, 42, 49, 61, 68. Describe the native host boundary and assess product and core-standard impacts at 1979-12-31. Dedicated memory and other unrelated accessories explicitly carry no direct impact. Conditional comparisons do not establish qualified adapters, provider adoption or measured sales. Prices and cumulative sales remain editorial evidence, outside foundation and the annual-sales model. See the per-item evidence in data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-peripherals-1979/assessment.json.

after.name: Apple Disk II
after.description: Apple Disk II is a storage peripheral for Apple II.

specification.description: Controller-driven 5¼-inch floppy system; the original 13-sector format stores about 114 KB per disk side. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

Assessment at 1979-12-31. These are conditional commercial comparisons, not measured changes in sales.

{primary_offering}: Disk II is the established same-host disk alternative; retaining Apple disk software can reduce migration work, while FlexiDisk II needs its recorded Apple interface and format qualification.

{related_offering}: The Logix card includes a Disk II-compatible controller path as well as FlexiBUS, so the installed Disk II ecosystem can complement the card as well as compete with a new external drive.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Compare an Apple II with working Disk II software against the 1979 Logix card and qualified FlexiDisk II configuration.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Disk II uses an Apple controller/disk interface rather than FlexiBUS; disk-format compatibility alone does not convert the transport.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Existing disks and applications create a switching hurdle. Retaining a qualified Disk II path can make incremental FlexiBUS adoption more attractive; no sales uplift is measured.

after.name: Radio Shack Mini-Disk 26-1160
after.description: Radio Shack Mini-Disk 26-1160 is a storage peripheral for TRS-80 Model I Expansion Interface.

specification.description: Single-density 5¼-inch floppy drive for the Model I disk subsystem. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.
Assessment at 1979-12-31. The accessory is tied to the named third-party platform. No qualified Logix attachment or same-host Logix substitute is established, so no direct product impact is assigned.
Assessment at 1979-12-31. The native host interface does not implement a core Logix/AION standard. A possible future bridge is not an existing implementation or adoption effect.

after.name: Realistic CTR-41 cassette recorder
after.description: Realistic CTR-41 cassette recorder is a storage peripheral for TRS-80 and suitable cassette-interface micros.

specification.description: Consumer audio recorder used for program storage through the host's cassette interface. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

Assessment at 1979-12-31. Cassette storage supports its own host workflow. No cassette-based Logix product or qualified cassette bridge is recorded; it is not a drop-in replacement for FlexiDisk. No direct product impact is assigned.
Assessment at 1979-12-31. Audio recording formats and transport control are not the FlexiBUS disk class. Shared use of a serial or cassette connection establishes no standards adoption.

after.name: North Star Micro-Disk System
after.description: North Star Micro-Disk System is a storage peripheral for S-100 systems.

specification.description: Hard-sectored 5¼-inch floppy system combining drive, controller and software. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

Assessment at 1979-12-31. These are conditional commercial comparisons, not measured changes in sales.

{primary_offering}: A working native disk controller provides an alternative to buying a FlexiBUS host card for storage; both paths require host-specific qualification.

{related_offering}: On a suitably configured S-100 host, native disk storage is a competing purchase path. Capacity, boot support and disk formats must be compared separately; a controller alone is not a complete drive.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Compare complete usable S-100 disk configurations, including the drive, controller, boot path and operating-system driver.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: Native controller registers and disk timing differ from FlexiBUS sector messages. Existing CP/M disk formats do not establish host-bus or media interchangeability.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Installed disks and BIOS support can hold users to native controllers. FlexiBUS offers a conditional cross-host reuse argument, subject to throughput and recovery qualification rather than assumed superiority.
